original_question: Which k-orbit polytopes P admit a universal k-orbit extension that covers every other k-orbit extension of P?
target_in_paper: The paper’s open problem on “Universal Extensions?” in its combinatorial-constructions discussion: for a k-orbit abstract polytope P, whether there is a universal k-orbit extension of P with the usual universal cover/quotient property. ([matmor.unam.mx](https://matmor.unam.mx/SIGMAP/talks/SIGMAP2018Cunningham.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft captures the core mathematical intent correctly: it is about k-orbit polytopes, extensions of a fixed polytope P, and a universal object that dominates all other such extensions by a covering map. That is exactly the content suggested by the paper’s “Universal Extensions?” problem. ([matmor.unam.mx](https://matmor.unam.mx/SIGMAP/talks/SIGMAP2018Cunningham.pdf))
missing_details: The paper is about k-orbit abstract polytopes, not specifically convex or geometric polytopes; P should be identified as an abstract d-polytope. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1608.07993))

An extension of P should be made explicit as an abstract (d+1)-polytope all of whose facets are isomorphic to P. This is the standard nearby meaning of “extension” used by the same authors’ surrounding literature on extensions. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7166217/developments-and-open-problems-on-chiral-polytopes))
The orbit condition on the extension should be stated explicitly: the extension sought is itself k-orbit. ([matmor.unam.mx](https://matmor.unam.mx/SIGMAP/talks/SIGMAP2018Cunningham.pdf))

The universal property should define “covers” precisely; in this line of work, a cover is given combinatorially by a color-preserving graph epimorphism between flag graphs. ([matmor.unam.mx](https://matmor.unam.mx/SIGMAP/talks/SIGMAP2018Cunningham.pdf))
The rank shift should be stated: if P has rank d, the extension has rank d+1. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7166217/developments-and-open-problems-on-chiral-polytopes))

It helps to say whether the problem is existential for each fixed P (“does there exist…?”) rather than classificatory in full generality (“which P?”). The paper’s formulation appears as an existence-style open problem tag rather than a full classification theorem. ([matmor.unam.mx](https://matmor.unam.mx/SIGMAP/talks/SIGMAP2018Cunningham.pdf))
No ambient field, ring, degree, homogeneity, or analytic conditions are relevant here; this is a purely combinatorial abstract-polytope question.
refined_question: Given a k-orbit abstract d-polytope P, does there exist a k-orbit abstract (d+1)-polytope U whose facets are all isomorphic to P such that, for every other k-orbit abstract (d+1)-polytope Q with facets isomorphic to P, U covers Q; that is, there is a color-preserving epimorphism from the flag graph of U onto the flag graph of Q? ([matmor.unam.mx](https://matmor.unam.mx/SIGMAP/talks/SIGMAP2018Cunningham.pdf))
justification: The draft is clearly targeting the paper’s “Universal Extensions?” item, which appears in the authors’ presentation of the same open-problem program under “Combinatorial constructions.” ([matmor.unam.mx](https://matmor.unam.mx/SIGMAP/talks/SIGMAP2018Cunningham.pdf)) The paper itself is a survey of open problems on k-orbit abstract polytopes, so the refined version should stay in the abstract/combinatorial category rather than drifting to convex or geometric realizations. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1608.07993)) Because the paper extract available through web search does not expose the full prose of that specific problem, the sharpest stand-alone reconstruction uses the standard local meaning of “extension” and “universal extension” from the closely adjacent regular/chiral extension literature cited and used by the same community: an extension of a d-polytope is a (d+1)-polytope whose facets are isomorphic to the original polytope, and a universal extension is one covering or quotienting onto every other extension of the same kind. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/7166217/developments-and-open-problems-on-chiral-polytopes)) The covering relation is made explicit using the authors’ own definition from the related SIGMAP talk: a color-preserving graph epimorphism of flag graphs. ([matmor.unam.mx](https://matmor.unam.mx/SIGMAP/talks/SIGMAP2018Cunningham.pdf))
